Walmart announced it will officially begin supporting Apple Pay next week. The retailer has refused to offer Apple Pay support for years, despite pressure from customers.

Apple Pay finally lands at Walmart

Walmart announced the news in a press release today. Starting August 24, the company will陆续 roll out contactless payment options, including Apple Pay, at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations. The feature will cover all U.S. stores by the end of this year and expand to gas stations by mid-2027.

Walmart is adding broad contactless payment support, covering Apple Pay and Google Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, contactless credit cards, and other payment platforms. Customers can also add Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to Apple Wallet and other platforms. Contactless payments will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart Pay.

The company stated:

Walmart is one of the last major retailers to迟迟 not support Apple Pay, and this is significant news for consumers. For years, the retailer has refused to offer contactless payment features, insisting on its own QR code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

Last year, Walmart still firmly believed that Walmart Pay provided a more convenient experience for customers than Apple Pay. However, using Walmart Pay requires first adding a debit or credit card to the Walmart app on iPhone, then scanning a QR code at checkout to pay with iPhone.

A quick search on social media reveals just how frustrated customers are with Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, other retailers that long resisted Apple Pay have gradually relented over the years, including Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B — and there's a reason for that.

Would Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support affect your shopping habits? When Walmart and Sam's Club launch Apple Pay, will you be more inclined to shop there? Let us know in the comments.
